unit.title: Maintain quality systems within a team

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: In an electrical contracting firm, what is the quality system?
options: The procedures, checks and records that keep work right
The list of hand tools that each worker must own and carry
The price list that the firm sends to its clients
The rules on what uniform the staff must wear

questions.stem: Which document tells a worker exactly how to do one task, such as terminating an armoured cable?
options: The firm's quality policy statement
A work instruction
The supplier's invoice for the cable
The delivery note for the job

questions.stem: A framed, signed quality policy hangs on the wall of the firm's office. What is that document?
options: A list of the insurance cover the firm holds
The step-by-step method for doing each job
A short statement of the firm's quality aims
The record of test results for a single job

questions.stem: Why must old copies of a procedure be taken out of use when a new revision is issued?
options: So the office has more room on its shelves
So the new copy looks more important
So the auditor has fewer pages to read
So nobody works to out-of-date steps

questions.stem: How can a worker tell whether the procedure in his hand is the current one?
options: Check its revision and date against the master list
See whether the paper looks new, clean and freshly printed
Ask the client if it is the right one
Check whether it is printed in colour

questions.stem: Which of these is a quality record?
options: A blank inspection form in the drawer
A signed test sheet for a finished circuit
An advert from a cable supplier
The fuel receipt for the van

questions.stem: Why must quality records be kept for a set time after a job?
options: So the office has old paper to recycle
So the workers can be paid twice for it
To prove the work was checked, if questioned
So the same job can be done over again

questions.stem: Who is responsible for quality in an electrical team?
options: Only the inspector, at the very end of the job
Only the owner of the firm, from the office
Only the client, who checks the work
Everyone, with the leader checking the system

questions.stem: What is the team leader's main quality task each day?
options: Making sure procedures and checks are followed
Doing every single inspection personally and alone
Writing a brand-new procedure every day
Signing all the records without looking

questions.stem: The manager asks each wiring team to report its quality KPIs every month. What is a KPI?
options: The key that opens the firm's store room
A measure, such as the first-time pass rate
The name of the best worker of the month
The price that is charged for a job

questions.stem: A team had 40 circuits inspected, and 36 passed first time. What is the first-time pass rate?
The firm's quality officer books an internal audit of your wiring team for next week. What will it be?
options: A surprise visit from the power company
An insulation test on a single circuit
A count of the money in the cash box
A planned check that the system is followed

questions.stem: An auditor asks to see how your team records torque settings on board terminals. What is the best response?
options: Show the real records and explain the method
Write up some records quickly before showing
Say that you do not know anything about it
Ask the auditor to come back next year

questions.stem: Several board terminations are found loose at inspection. What does a 'corrective action' do?
options: It only tightens these particular terminations
It removes the cause so it does not come back
It records the problem and then closes the file
It keeps the problem hidden from the client

questions.stem: What is 'preventive action'?
options: Action taken after a client has complained
Fixing a fault after a test has failed
Action to stop a possible problem early
Writing a report after an accident

questions.stem: After repeated complaints of tripping breakers, the team uses the '5 whys'. What does this method do?
options: It checks five circuits in each board
It chooses five suppliers for each job
It writes five lines in every report
It finds a root cause by asking why again

questions.stem: Several outlets were wired with reversed polarity. Asking 'why' shows that new team members were never shown the conductor colours. What is the root cause?
options: A gap in training for new members
A faulty batch of socket outlets
A broken tester used on the job
The client asked for it to be done that way

questions.stem: What is a fishbone (cause-and-effect) diagram used for?
options: Showing the route of a long cable run
Sorting a problem's possible causes
Planning the order of tasks on a job
Showing the layout of a distribution board

questions.stem: Your team tries a new board-labelling method using Plan–Do–Check–Act. What does the team do at the third step?
options: The change is tried out on a small scale first
The problem is described and a change planned
Results are measured against the plan
The change is made the standard way of working

questions.stem: Which is an example of continuous improvement in a team?
options: Doing every job the same way for ever
Changing procedures without telling anyone
Removing an inspection step to save time
Trying a new labelling method; keeping it if errors fall

questions.stem: Why does the quality system keep a register of all test instruments and their calibration due dates?
options: So no instrument is used past its due date
So the instruments can be sold off later at a profit
So the store knows the colour of each one
So workers can take them home at weekends

questions.stem: An insulation tester fails its calibration check. What must be done about jobs it was used on since its last good check?
options: Nothing, because those jobs are now finished
Review those results and retest where needed
Throw away the old records for those jobs
Ask the clients whether they had any problems

questions.stem: How does client feedback fit into a quality system?
options: It is filed away and never read again
It replaces the need for any inspection
It is recorded and reviewed to find improvements
It is only ever used for advertising

questions.stem: Why does the firm keep a record of the training and assessments each electrician on the team has passed?
options: To decide who may park closest to the gate
To keep a note of each person's home address
So that training is never needed again
To show each person is trained for their tasks

questions.stem: Before a shop rewire starts, the team leader receives the job's inspection and test plan. What does it set out?
options: What is checked, when, by whom, and against what
The price list for all of the firm's test equipment
A drawing that shows all the cable routes
The team's holiday dates for the year

questions.stem: What is the best use of a short weekly team quality meeting?
options: To read out who made the most mistakes
To review defects and agree improvements
To plan the firm's end-of-year party for the staff
To choose a new style of uniform

questions.stem: Why should team members feel free to report their own mistakes?
options: So they can be punished more quickly
So the records look busier than before
Problems are then found and fixed early
So the client pays for the repair work

questions.stem: A month's tally shows 18 defects: 11 unlabelled cables, 4 loose screws and 3 missing covers. Where should the team focus first?
options: Loose screws
Missing covers
All three equally
Cable labelling

questions.stem: What does a Pareto chart show?
options: Problems from the most to the least frequent
Cable sizes in order of their cost per metre
Tasks in order of their planned start dates
Workers in order of their rates of pay

questions.stem: Why does the quality system refer to the wiring code the Centre uses?
options: It sets the prices the firm may charge
It sets the technical rules the work must meet
It tells the firm which brands to buy
It sets the hours that staff must work

questions.stem: How does the quality system help stop poor materials reaching the job?
options: By buying the cheapest items every time
By letting each worker buy their own
Approved suppliers and checks on arrival
By checking items only after fitting

questions.stem: A team member finds a better way to do a task. How should the written procedure be changed?
options: Just start doing it, and tell no one
Change the copy in the van by hand
Wait for the auditor to suggest it
Propose it, get approval, update and brief

questions.stem: Why does a second person sometimes check a critical connection, such as the main earth?
options: A second check catches what the first missed
So the first person can go home a little early that day
So the job takes twice as long to do
So the record has two names, just for show

questions.stem: Why is rework a concern in a quality system?
options: It earns extra money for the firm each time
It wastes time and materials and upsets clients
It is never needed as long as the client is happy
It only affects the people in the office

questions.stem: Rework cost J$45 000 on a job worth J$900 000. What percentage of the job's value is that?
How should a tester that is waiting for repair be marked and kept?
options: With nothing, left in the toolbox as normal
With tape stuck over its display only
With a note left in the van's glove box
Tagged 'out of service', and kept apart

questions.stem: Where does the team find the client's quality requirements for a job?
options: In the contract, specification and drawings
In the supplier's latest product catalogue and price list
In the team's group chat on their phones
In the files from last year's jobs

questions.stem: An internal audit finds three test sheets that were never signed. What should the team leader do?
options: Sign them himself without checking anything
Have them checked and signed, and find out why
Throw the three sheets away and start again
Ignore it, because the tests themselves were carried out

questions.stem: How is safe isolation part of the quality system as well as safety?
options: It is needed only when the auditor visits
It is left to each worker to decide
It is a written procedure that is followed and recorded
It replaces the need for any testing

questions.stem: Which is the best way for a team leader to keep the team committed to quality?
options: Punish every mistake in front of everyone
Check the work only when the boss visits
Leave quality to the inspector at the end
Explain why checks matter; praise good work

questions.stem: What should happen to a drawing that has been marked up on site to show changes?
options: Returned so the as-built drawings are updated
Thrown away once the job has been finished and paid
Kept folded in one worker's back pocket
Given to the supplier with the next order

questions.stem: Which data would best show whether a new training session reduced wiring errors?
options: How many people used the staff canteen during that week
Defect counts before and after the training
The cost of hiring the training room
The running time of the training video

questions.stem: A client complaint about a flickering light is logged in the quality system. Why?
options: So the client can be blamed for the fault
So the log book looks full when audited
So the cause is found and others prevented
So that nobody has to visit the client

questions.stem: Why does the team use the same checklist for every board it installs?
options: So the job takes longer than it needs to
So all the boards are the same colour
So the workers need no training at all
So nothing is missed and results compare

questions.stem: A non-conformance report about a missing earth connection has been raised. At what point may it be closed?
options: When the fix is checked and shown to work
As soon as the report has been written
When the client stops phoning the office
At the end of the year, with all the others

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In the Plan–Do–Check–Act cycle, which step comes straight after 'Do'?
What is the master list that shows the current revision of every procedure and form called?
What two-word term means the deepest, underlying reason a problem happened?
Of 50 boards installed, 2 needed rework. What percentage needed rework?
What is it called when a job has to be done again because it was wrong the first time?
Which document tells the client in writing that the installation was tested and the results were satisfactory?
What do we call the form a worker fills in to report work or material that does not meet a requirement? (words or letters)
Test sheets must be kept for 5 years after a job. A job ended in 2026. Until what year are its sheets kept?
Some electrical firms borrow a Japanese term for steady, small-step betterment of the way work is done. What is the word?
What word describes a worker's proven ability to do a task to the required standard?
Thirty-two of 40 clients rated the service 'good'. What percentage is that?
What is the set period between one calibration of a test instrument and the next called?
What word describes a document that has been withdrawn and replaced by a newer revision?
Defects fell from 20 last month to 15 this month. By what percentage did they fall?
What is the term for the checks a worker makes on their own work before passing it on?

essays.stem: Explain what a quality system is in an electrical contracting firm, and describe its main parts.
essays.modelAnswer: A quality system is the organised way a firm makes sure its work meets the client's requirements and the wiring code every time, not just by luck. Its main parts are: a quality policy, which states the firm's aims; procedures and work instructions, which say how tasks such as safe isolation, terminating cables and testing are done; and forms and checklists for inspection and testing. Records, such as test sheets, inspection reports and calibration certificates, prove what was done. Document control makes sure everyone uses the current drawings and procedures. Control of test instruments keeps them calibrated. Training records show people are competent. There are ways to deal with problems: non-conformance reports, corrective and preventive action. Finally, audits, client feedback and team meetings check the system works and drive improvement.
markingPoints: Defines the quality system as an organised way to meet requirements consistently
Policy, procedures, work instructions and checklists
Records and document control
Instrument control and training records
Non-conformance, corrective and preventive action, audits, feedback and improvement

essays.stem: Describe the team leader's role in keeping the quality system working in a team of electricians.
essays.modelAnswer: The team leader makes sure everyone in the team knows the procedures that apply to their work and has the current drawings and work instructions. He checks that each person is trained and competent for the tasks given, and arranges coaching where they are not. Each day he checks that the agreed inspections and tests are done at the right stages, that safe isolation is followed, and that records are filled in correctly, signed and handed in. He checks that test instruments are in calibration and that faulty ones are tagged and withdrawn. When a problem is found he makes sure it is recorded, made safe and corrected, and helps find the root cause. He holds short quality meetings, shares results and listens to ideas. He sets an example by following the system himself and encourages people to report mistakes without fear.
markingPoints: Makes sure the team knows and has current procedures and drawings
Checks competence and arranges training
Checks inspections, tests, safe isolation and records daily
Controls instruments; ensures problems are recorded, corrected and root cause found
Holds meetings, sets an example and builds an open culture

essays.stem: Explain how document control works and why it matters when drawings and procedures change during a job.
essays.modelAnswer: Document control means every controlled document, such as a drawing, specification or procedure, has a number, a revision letter or number and a date, and is listed on a master register. Only approved documents are issued, and the register records who holds a copy. When a document changes, the new revision is approved, issued to everyone who holds a copy, and the old copies are collected and destroyed or clearly marked 'superseded'. Workers check the revision on their copy against the register before using it. Marked-up changes made on site are sent back so the master and the as-built drawings are updated. This matters because if one electrician works from an old drawing, he may put outlets or circuits in the wrong place, or use the wrong cable size, causing rework, delays, failed inspections or danger.
markingPoints: Documents numbered, revised, dated and listed on a register
New revisions approved and issued to all holders
Old copies withdrawn or marked superseded
Workers check revisions; site mark-ups returned for as-builts
Explains the risks of using old documents

essays.stem: A client reports that several outlets in a new building have no earth connection. Describe how the team would deal with this through the quality system, from the report to closing it.
essays.modelAnswer: This is a serious safety problem, so the first step is to make it safe: the affected circuits are isolated, locked off and tagged, and the client is told not to use them. The complaint is logged and a non-conformance report is raised. The team leader sends a competent electrician to inspect and test all the outlets in the building, not just the ones reported, and records the findings. The faults are corrected and every circuit is retested dead before the supply is restored by the authorised person. The team then looks for the root cause, for example by asking 'why' several times: perhaps earth conductors were not connected at second fix and the dead tests were skipped or not recorded. Corrective action removes that cause, such as retraining and adding an earth continuity check to the checklist. The report is closed only when the fix is checked and the action has been shown to work.
markingPoints: Makes safe first by isolation; informs the client
Logs the complaint and raises a non-conformance report
Inspects and tests all outlets, corrects and retests before restoring supply
Finds the root cause
Takes corrective action and closes only when proved effective

essays.stem: On an electrical job, how do a correction, a corrective action and a preventive action differ? Use one electrical example for each.
essays.modelAnswer: A correction fixes the problem that has been found, without dealing with why it happened. For example, an inspector finds a loose neutral in a board and the electrician tightens it. Corrective action goes further: it finds and removes the cause of a problem that has already happened, so it does not happen again. For example, loose terminals keep being found, the cause is traced to worn screwdrivers and no torque figure in the procedure, so torque screwdrivers are issued and the procedure is updated. Preventive action deals with a problem that has not happened yet but could. For example, the team notices that a new type of outlet has small terminals that could be hard to tighten, so before using them they practise on samples and add a check to the checklist. Correction is needed straight away; corrective and preventive action improve the system.
markingPoints: Correction fixes the found problem only, with example
Corrective action removes the cause of an actual problem, with example
Preventive action deals with a possible problem before it happens, with example
Shows how they differ and why each is needed

essays.stem: Describe how you would use the Plan–Do–Check–Act cycle to reduce labelling errors in distribution boards.
essays.modelAnswer: Plan: I would collect the facts, such as how many boards had labelling errors at inspection over the last two months, and what kinds of error. With the team I would find the likely causes, for example no standard format and labels written at the end of the day in a hurry. We would plan a change: a pre-printed label sheet that matches the circuit schedule, filled in as each circuit is terminated, and a check by a second person. We would set a target, such as halving the errors. Do: we would try the new method on the next few boards and train the team to use it. Check: we would count the labelling errors at inspection on those boards and compare them with before. Act: if the errors fell, we would make the method standard, update the procedure and brief everyone; if not, we would look again and start a new cycle.
markingPoints: Plan: collects data, finds causes, plans a change with a target
Do: tries the change on a small scale and trains the team
Check: measures results and compares with before
Act: makes it standard and updates the procedure, or repeats the cycle

essays.stem: Explain how the quality system controls test instruments, and what happens when an instrument is found to be faulty.
essays.modelAnswer: Each test instrument, such as an insulation tester, low-resistance ohmmeter, voltage indicator and proving unit, has its own number and is listed on a register with its calibration due date. It is sent for calibration at the set interval and carries a label showing the date. Users check the label before use and do simple checks: leads undamaged, battery good, leads nulled, and the voltage indicator proved on a proving unit before and after use. Instruments are stored and carried carefully. If an instrument is found faulty or out of calibration, it is taken out of use at once, tagged 'out of service' and kept apart. The team leader is told and a report is made. The records are checked to find every job it was used on since its last good check, and those results are reviewed and the circuits retested where needed. The instrument is repaired and recalibrated before it is used again.
markingPoints: Register with numbers and due dates; calibrated at set intervals and labelled
Checks before use, including proving unit before and after
Faulty instrument withdrawn, tagged and kept apart, and reported
Past results since the last good check reviewed and retested
Repaired and recalibrated before reuse

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare your team for an internal quality audit, and how you would respond to its findings.
essays.modelAnswer: I would explain to the team that an audit checks the system, not the people, and that it helps us improve. Before the audit I would check that our documents are the current revisions, that records such as test sheets, inspection reports and isolation records are complete and signed, and that instruments are in calibration and labelled. I would make sure everyone knows where the procedures are and can explain how they do their tasks. I would not create records after the event or hide problems. During the audit the team should answer honestly and show what they actually do. After the audit I would go through the findings with the team. For each one we would correct the problem, find the root cause and agree an action with a date and a person responsible. I would record the actions, check that they are done and tell the auditor, so each finding can be closed.
markingPoints: Explains the purpose of the audit to the team
Checks documents, records and instruments beforehand
Team knows procedures; honest answers; no faking records
Reviews findings, corrects and finds root causes, with actions, dates and owners
Records, follows up and closes findings

essays.stem: Explain how measures such as pass rates, rework and complaints can be collected and used to improve a team's work.
essays.modelAnswer: Measures turn opinions into facts. I would collect them from records the team already keeps: inspection results give the first-time pass rate and the types of defect; job cards and timesheets show the hours and materials spent on rework; the complaint log and client feedback show what clients notice. Each month I would put the figures in a simple table or chart, such as the percentage of circuits passing first time and a Pareto chart of the most common defects. I would share the results at the team quality meeting. The chart shows where to focus, for example if most defects are unlabelled cables. The team would then find the cause and agree a change. In the following months we would watch the same measures to see if the change worked. Good results should be recognised, so the team sees that quality matters.
markingPoints: Measures give facts
Collects from inspection records, rework hours and complaints
Presents results monthly, e.g. pass rate and Pareto chart
Uses results to choose a focus and agree a change
Watches later results and recognises good work

essays.stem: Explain how training and competence records support quality, and how a team leader can build a team culture where people report problems.
essays.modelAnswer: Training and competence records show what each person has been trained and assessed to do, such as safe isolation, terminating boards or testing. The team leader uses them to give each task to someone competent and to plan training where there are gaps. If a fault is traced to a gap in skills, the records show it and the training can be fixed. Auditors and clients can also see that the team is qualified. A good quality culture is one where people report mistakes and near misses early, because hidden problems can become dangerous. The team leader builds this by thanking people who report problems, never shouting or blaming in public, and focusing on fixing the cause rather than the person. He explains why each check matters, involves the team in solving problems, shares results openly and follows the system himself.
markingPoints: Records show who is trained and competent for each task
Used to allocate tasks and plan training; help trace skills gaps
Show competence to auditors and clients
Explains why reporting problems early matters
Leader thanks reporters, avoids blame, focuses on causes, involves the team and sets an example

practical1.title: Quality check and root-cause investigation on a team's installation work
practical1.brief: The assessor provides two or three completed installations on the Centre's training boards (dead and never connected to a supply), each with some built-in defects, and a month of made-up defect records for an imaginary team. As a quality team: (1) agree an inspection checklist and the pass limit for each line; (2) carry out and record safe isolation of each training board (switch off, lock off, tag, prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after); (3) inspect the installations and carry out protective conductor continuity tests with a calibrated instrument, recording every result; (4) raise a non-conformance report for each defect; (5) use the month's records to draw a Pareto chart of defect types; (6) choose the biggest problem and find its root cause with a '5 whys' or fishbone diagram; and (7) write a corrective and a preventive action with an owner and date. Present the findings to the assessor, who acts as the firm's manager. Each member leads one step and checks another member's work. Photograph each stage.
materials: Two or three training-board installations with built-in defects (not connected to any supply)
A month of made-up defect records (from the assessor)
Lock-off kit, danger tags, voltage indicator and proving unit
Low-resistance ohmmeter or multifunction tester with a calibration label in date
Inspection checklists, record sheets and non-conformance report forms
Graph paper or a computer for the Pareto chart, flip chart and markers
photos: The agreed checklist with pass limits
A training board locked off and tagged, and the tester being checked
The completed record sheets and non-conformance reports
The corrective and preventive actions being presented
checklist: Carried out safe isolation correctly before inspecting
Checked the instrument's calibration and nulled the leads before testing
Found and recorded the built-in defects accurately
Drew an accurate Pareto chart from the records
Found a sensible root cause and wrote clear actions with owners and dates
Presented their part clearly and checked another member's work
safety: The training boards stay dead throughout; only the instructor may energise anything
Prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after, with each member's own lock and tag
Use insulated tools in good condition and keep the area tidy
Follow the maker's instructions for each instrument and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Set up and audit a team's quality documents
practical2.brief: As a group, build a small quality file for an imaginary electrical team. It must include: (1) a document register listing each document with its number, revision and date; (2) a one-page work instruction for terminating a cable into a socket outlet, with a photo or sketch of each step; (3) an instrument register with calibration due dates for the Centre's test instruments; (4) a training and competence matrix for five team members; and (5) a short inspection checklist for a finished outlet circuit. Test the work instruction: one member who did not write it follows it exactly on a training board that is never connected to a supply, after safe isolation is carried out and recorded, while the others note any step that is unclear; then revise the instruction to revision B and update the register. Finally, swap files with another group (or use the assessor's file) and carry out a mock internal audit: check revisions, records, calibration dates and competence against the tasks, and write an audit report with findings. Each member leads one document and takes part in the audit. Photograph each stage.
materials: Computer with word processing or spreadsheet software, or paper forms
A training board (not connected to any supply), a socket outlet, a short length of cable and hand tools
Lock-off kit, danger tags, voltage indicator and proving unit
List of the Centre's test instruments and their calibration labels
Audit checklist and audit report forms
photos: The work instruction being tested on the training board
The revised work instruction and updated register (revision B)
The instrument register and the competence matrix
checklist: Led one document and made it clear, correct and controlled
Wrote or followed the work instruction exactly and noted unclear steps
Revised the instruction and updated the register correctly
Recorded calibration dates and spotted any instrument out of date
Took part in the audit and found real findings, not opinions
Wrote findings clearly with the evidence for each
Worked safely during the practical test of the instruction
safety: The training board is never connected to a supply; only the instructor may energise anything
Carry out safe isolation before the work instruction is tested: off, lock, tag, prove dead with a tester checked before and after
Use insulated tools in good condition; wear safety glasses when stripping cable
Keep laptop cables and bags off the floor
